land.text: the western half, west of the Tarum (Citarum) River: 'Tarusbawa ... founded a capital near the Cipakancilan river, near modern Bogor'

successors.note: Galuh page: 'In 670, Tarumanagara was divided into the Sunda Kingdom (west) and the Galuh Kingdom (east)'. Cliopatria's Tarumanagara runs to 673 and its Sunda row starts 674.

land.text: the eastern half, east of the Citarum

successors.note: Founded in 612 within Tarumanagara by Wretikandayun, 'a breakaway kingdom' around 669.

capitals.name: Sundapura
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Sundapura, between North Jakarta and Bekasi Regency'; under Suryawarman (535-561) Sundapura 'became a smaller vassal kingdom called Sunda Sambawa when he moved the capital east'. The new seat is not named on the page, so the dot stays at Sundapura.

correction.text: Greater Jakarta, Bogor and Bekasi with Banten: Cliopatria's 367 shape held from 358

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox gives 'Established: ca. 358 AD' (the earliest inscriptions 'estimated to date from around 358 AD') and Cliopatria starts the Jakarta-Bogor-Banten shape in 367. The shape is Cliopatria's 367 shape unchanged.

17,409 km2 for 367-533: the page puts the kingdom 'in and around modern-day Bogor, Bekasi and Jakarta', roughly the Greater Jakarta area, with Batujaya (Karawang) inside its territory and the Cidanghiang inscription at Lebak, south of Banten. The Purnawarman page (reign 395-434, infobox) has the kingdom in 'West Java, Jakarta, and Banten provinces', the capital 'somewhere near present-day Tugu' or Bekasi, and calls the Wangsakerta claim of 48 small kingdoms (to Purbalingga) a 20th-century forgery. No infobox area.

33,369 km2 for 534-611, which doubles the shape. The page has Manikmaya founding Kendan near Nagreg in 526 and Suryawarman (535-561) moving the capital east, leaving Sundapura as the vassal Sunda Sambawa; it gives no extent for either.

62,499 km2 for 612-665: the shape adds the Galuh country east of the Citarum in 612, the very year the page has Wretikandayun found the Galuh Kingdom ('In 612, his grandson Wretikandayun founded the Galuh Kingdom'); the Galuh page calls Galuh a 'breakaway kingdom' of Tarumanagara around 669. The 612 shape is exactly Cliopatria's Sunda 674 shape (89 cells) plus its Galuh 674 shape (136 cells). Read as Tarumanagara with Galuh as its dependency (a vassal tint) to 669.

correction.text: unchanged shape, for 666-669 only; from 670 it is divided between the Sunda Kingdom and the Galuh Kingdom

keyframe_review.note: 62,499 km2, the same shape, for 666-673. The page's infobox gives 'Invasion by Sriwijaya: 669 AD' and 'existed between 358 and 669 CE' (its text also dates the attack 'very likely' to c. 686, from the Kota Kapur stone); 666 matches the To-lo-mo embassy of 666, which the page's footnotes assign to Dandan. The shape holds to 669 only; from 670 the land is Sunda (west) and Galuh (east).

region.text: Greater Jakarta: 'in and around modern-day Bogor, Bekasi and Jakarta'

ledger.note: 358: Tarumanagara appears around Sundapura. Infobox 'Established: ca. 358 AD', 'Preceded by: Buni culture'; the page places it 'in and around modern-day Bogor, Bekasi and Jakarta'.

region.text: the land added to the Jakarta-Bogor shape in Cliopatria's 534 shape

ledger.note: c. 534: the shape widens (Cliopatria's year; the page is silent on a conquest). Manikmaya left Sundapura for Kendan near Nagreg in 526 and Suryawarman (535-561) moved the capital east.

535: Suryawarman moves the capital east. 'Under Suryawarman (535-561), Sundapura became a smaller vassal kingdom called Sunda Sambawa when he moved the capital east'; the page does not name the new seat.

region.text: the Galuh country east of the Citarum

ledger.note: 612: Wretikandayun founds Galuh inside Tarumanagara's sphere. 'In 612, his grandson Wretikandayun founded the Galuh Kingdom'; the Galuh page calls it 'a breakaway kingdom' of Tarumanagara around 669. Cliopatria draws the Galuh country as Tarumanagara's from 612; the vassal status is a reading.

669: Galuh breaks away. Infobox 'Separation from Tarumanagara by Wretikandayun: 669 AD'; the text has 'In 670, Tarumanagara was divided into the Sunda Kingdom (west) and the Galuh Kingdom (east), separated by the Tarum (Citarum) River'.

669: Srivijaya's invasion ends Tarumanagara. Infobox 'Invasion by Sriwijaya: 669 AD'; 'coastal Banten and Jakarta areas came under Srivijayan control after the invasion', Tarusbawa moved inland and founded a capital near Bogor, and the Galuh page divides the realm in 670. The page also says Tarumanagara was 'very likely' attacked around 686 (Kota Kapur), which contradicts 669.

wars.name: Srivijayan invasion of Tarumanagara

zones.text: 'coastal Banten and Jakarta areas came under Srivijayan control after the invasion'

wars.outcome: Tarumanagara falls; Tarusbawa moves inland to Bogor; the Galuh page has the realm divided into Sunda and Galuh in 670; the coast came under Srivijaya.
wars.note: The infobox dates the invasion 669; the text says Tarumanagara was 'very likely' attacked around 686, citing the Kota Kapur inscription (28 February 686), which names 'bhumi java' without naming Tarumanagara and 'does not give the outcome' (Kota Kapur page). Linggawarman (628-650) left only daughters, who married Tarusbawa and Srivijaya's Dapunta Hyang. The war is closed at 669, the end of Tarumanagara's life; the c. 686 reading stays in this note.

certainty.note: Inscriptions in Bogor, Jakarta, Bekasi, Karawang and Lebak give places, never a frontier.

notes: Start 358 (infobox ca. 358; the rulers listed by the Wangsakerta manuscripts, which the page calls likely fraudulent, are not used and no ruler strip is given). End 669 (infobox 'Invasion by Sriwijaya: 669 AD'); Cliopatria runs to 673 and the Galuh page has the division in 670. The page's text gives c. 686 for the Srivijayan attack, from the Kota Kapur stone, which does not name Tarumanagara: unresolved. Cliopatria's 612 shape (62,499 km2) adds the Galuh country in the year the page has Galuh founded; read here as a dependency, not as the same state. The coastal strip is unresolved: the page gives coastal Banten and Jakarta to Srivijaya after the invasion, while Cliopatria keeps it in Sunda's shape 674-723 (and its Srivijaya shape of 692 holds no Banten or Jakarta cell). Counterparts without a dossier: Kendan (526-612), Sunda Sambawa (535-669), Salakanagara (Wangsakerta only, not used), Buni culture (infobox predecessor; an archaeological culture). Infobox gives no area. Pages opened: 5 of the budget of 5.
